subject: Hosted API transfers & subprocessor micro-explainer for product pages
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short, customer-facing blurb on transfers/subprocessors for our procurement page

Hi Vivek / Laura,

We need a very short, non-legal blurb (ideally 1–2 sentences) to put into ACME's procurement portal that explains how Redwood handles cross-border transfers and subprocessors for the Hosted API. Procurement flagged three items: SCCs/UK Addendum, an up-to-date subprocessor list, and whether we offer customer-managed keys or residency options.

Can you provide two short options: one procurement-facing (slightly more detail) and one consumer-facing (one sentence, plain English)? Also please attach any supporting DPA or subprocessor links we can include. Our legal team wants something we can paste into the portal by next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Sara Lin
Head of Cloud Procurement
ACME Corp

Attachment: acme_procurement_template.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-18T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short, customer-facing blurb on transfers/subprocessors for our procurement page

Sara — thanks, this is straightforward. Drafting two succinct options below plus links we can publish from the console. Attaching a quick draft doc for internal review.

Option A — procurement-facing (2 lines):
"Redwood Inference executes cross-border data transfers under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and UK Addendum where applicable, and maintains an up-to-date subprocessor list linked from our privacy center. Customers requiring data residency or dedicated isolation can choose Dedicated or Private deployments; customer-managed encryption keys are available for supported plans."

Option B — consumer-facing (one sentence):
"We protect your data with contractual safeguards for transfers, publish our subprocessor list publicly, and offer options for data residency and customer-managed keys."

Suggested links to include: DPA summary, live subprocessor list (console), and a short 'how transfers work' help doc.

Notes for legal: I used 'contractual safeguards' instead of enumerating SCCs in the consumer line — it keeps the tone non-technical. For procurement we called out SCCs/UK Addendum explicitly. Laura/Jonas — any quick legal/accuracy flags or word changes?

Attachment: hosted-transfers-draft_v1.docx

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short, customer-facing blurb on transfers/subprocessors for our procurement page

Thanks Vivek — good starting point. A couple of precision edits from privacy/legal: 

- For procurement copy, I recommend explicitly naming the mechanisms: "We transfer personal data under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (and any applicable UK Addendum) and rely on appropriate safeguards for other jurisdictions." That helps auditors.
- For the public/consumer line, "contractual safeguards" is fine, but add a parenthetical link to the live subprocessor list so procurement teams can see vendors.
- On keys: we should be careful with wording — "customer-managed encryption keys are available for supported plans" is correct, but add "via KMS integrations" to avoid implying all plans include it.
- Residency: call out "Dedicated or Private deployments" as the technical option rather than implying hosted can be region-locked by default.

Proposed procurement variant (edited):
"Redwood performs cross-border transfers under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and applicable UK Addendum; an up-to-date subprocessor list and DPA are linked from our privacy center. Customers with strict residency or key management requirements can opt for Dedicated or Private deployments (KMS integrations available)."

I also suggest a short console tooltip: "Transfers & subprocessors — See how we safeguard cross-border transfers and view our up-to-date list of subprocessors."

If that looks good I'll mark the draft as "privacy-reviewed" and Laura can coordinate with legal for final sign-off.

— Jonas, Head of Privacy (interim)
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short, customer-facing blurb on transfers/subprocessors for our procurement page

Thanks team — final copy suggestions and a slightly shorter procurement variant that procurement teams like. I also added two concise candidates we can drop into the product page and the console tooltip. See below.

Procurement-friendly (final candidate):
"Redwood Inference transfers personal data under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (and the UK Addendum where applicable). An up-to-date subprocessor list and our DPA are available from the privacy center. Customers needing data residency or customer-managed keys may choose Dedicated or Private deployments; KMS integrations are supported for eligible plans."

Public/product page (one-liner):
"We safeguard cross-border transfers with contractual controls and publish our subprocessor list; options for data residency and customer-managed keys are available."

Console tooltip (short):
"How transfers & subprocessors work — contractual safeguards, live subprocessor list, and deployment options for residency or key control."

Minor edits: replace 'contractual safeguards' with 'contractual controls' in the consumer line for clarity.

If we can get legal sign-off on the procurement wording, we can publish these as a linked snippet from the console and add the tooltip text to the Hosted API product page. Target: staging push on Thursday 6/24.

Attachment: snippet_final_candidates.txt

— Kimberly Park
Staff Product Writer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short, customer-facing blurb on transfers/subprocessors for our procurement page

Team — this looks good. Two very small asks before we paste into the portal: 
1) In the procurement copy, swap "KMS integrations are supported for eligible plans" to "customer-managed keys available" (procurement prefers direct phrasing).
2) Can you add a single link to the live subprocessor list (so the portal can link out)?

If you can make those two tiny edits I can paste into ACME's portal on Monday. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Sara
Head of Cloud Procurement, ACME Corp
